Youth robotics and AI

Children building robots and AI.

African children in Cameroon and Dallas–Fort Worth. A program of Glappy Foundation.

Partner with us See the 2027 plan

  • 5,000Children trained in Cameroon

Kids in Cameroon have been building and coding robots since November 2022. Source: AfroBot records, November 2026. Glappy Foundation’s Cameroon record reports the children learning now.

The problem

A shorter school week in Bamenda. A first season still ahead in Texas.

Cameroon

Kids in Bamenda were in school about four days a week because of the conflict there. Kids in other parts of the country were in school five days a week. Classes began in November 2022, under Glappy Foundation, so those children could keep learning to build.

Dallas–Fort Worth

In 2024, about 30 children in McKinney, Texas, built in five to six teams, with parents in the room.

Robotics and AI should not depend on a family’s income or zip code.

The model

Learn, build, and show the work.

  1. Learn

    Classes with a mentor. A child takes part through a parent or guardian. Mentors are screened before they meet students.

  2. Build

    Ages 6–12 start with a hands-on build. Ages 13–17 work toward a humanoid robot. In 2027, Dallas–Fort Worth teams build small humanoid robots from open-source schematics and 3D-printed parts.

  3. Show

    Training, safety, and a showcase. Dallas–Fort Worth and Yaoundé meet on separate dates. AfroBot is hosting the Yaoundé event.

See the programs for Discover through Advance.

Proof

Work that has already happened.

2027

Dallas–Fort Worth, at the scale of a season.

The 2024 pilot was about 30 children. The 2027 season is about 15 teams and about 90 students, with training, safety, and a showcase. The Cameroon program continues.

Interest is open. Sessions are not open for enrollment on this site yet. Other US regions, and a Dallas championship in April 2028, are proposed. Read that horizon.

Where we work

Two places.

Dallas–Fort Worth

The 2024 pilot was in McKinney. The 2027 season is about 15 teams and about 90 students.

Cameroon

Bamenda since November 2022. In 2027 AfroBot is hosting an event in Yaoundé, on a separate date from Dallas–Fort Worth.

The ask

Partner with us.

A partner can fund a child’s place, a team’s robot build, or training, safety, and the showcase. The camp-week participation goal is $100 per child. Sponsor goals are on the partners page.

Start a partnership inquiry partnerships@afrobot.org

To be added

Evidence this site does not have yet.

These items are marked on purpose. They are not implied by the counts above.

  • A theory of change.
  • Outcomes beyond headcount: who returns, what they can build, and the cost per child.
  • A 2027 budget and a use-of-funds note.
  • Founder and staff biographies.
  • Reflections from families or educators, with consent.
  • A confirmed partner list. No logos until then.
